newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends up on bullish data.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends up on bullish data.

text.p: Palm oil prices in Malaysia ended sharply higher after projections of larger falls in November output by local plantations houses triggered speculative and technical buying, traders said.
A Reuters poll of some Malaysian plantation houses on Thursday concluded that palm oil output in November could have fallen by up to 19 percent over a month ago.
The estimate was larger than the 14 percent fall projected by private crop forecaster Ivan Wong, and moved the market, traders said.
Output in October was 883,579 tonnes, the official Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) has said.
PORLA is expected to release its November crop data on Decemnber 16 while Wong is scheduled to make his next forecast on Friday.

"The fall in November production was expected," an executive at a plantation firm, responding to the Reuters poll, said on Thursday. "This is the seasonal downtrend in output. November, December, January and February are always the low crop months," he added.
"Technically, most futures were traded above the 1,200 ringgit level," a dealer said. "December futures is at a premium to other futures months."
Another dealer said players were trying to cover positions for January, February and March of 1997.
"So the market saw some speculative and technical buying activities in other futures contracts," he said.
At the close, December futures was up 21 ringgit at 1,212 ringgit ($480.57) a tonne, January futures up 16 at 1,207 and most active February futures up 15 at 1,210 ringgit.
With the increased buying interest and inter-months switching basis, the volume on the futures rose to 1,993 lots from 1,310 Wednesday.

Among physicals, Dec (south) crude palm oil was offered at 1,235 ringgit after trading from 1,215 to 1,230. Bids for Dec (south) was 1,230. Dec (central) saw offers at 1,225 and bids at 1,220, and Dec (north) at 1,220 against 1,210.
Jan (south) saw offers at 1,235 and bids at 1,232 with earlier trades at 1,225 and 1,230. Feb (south) was offered at 1,240 and bids at 1,230 after trading from 1,225 to 1,230.
Among refined products, Jan RBD palm oil was offered at $522.50 a tonne FOB Malaysia, and Feb/March at $520. Jan was traded $517.50.
Jan RBD palm olein saw offers at $560, Feb/Mar at $557.50. Jan was traded at $557.50.
Dec RBD palm stearin was offered at $377.50, Jan at $382.50 Feb/Mar at $387.50, and Dec/Jan palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $282.50. -- Tan Lee Lee - 603-230-7510 ($1 =2.5220 ringgit)
